publicly_readable: One article, reprinted on worldin.economist.com in 2015 for the 30th edition ("007 in 008", by John Grimond), read from an Internet Archive snapshot.
not_readable: Everything else in the issue. No other text of this edition was found in public form.

entries.quote: The second event will be the publication of a new Bond novel, “Devil May Care”, on May 28th.
entries.subject: New James Bond novel publication

entries.quote: We said the OPEC cartel would aim to keep oil prices in the lofty range of $60-80 a barrel
entries.subject: Oil price 2008
entries.note: Restated in the self-review "About 2008: sorry" in The World in 2009.

entries.quote: We thought that Romano Prodi would probably see out the year as prime minister of Italy
entries.subject: Italian prime minister

entries.quote: that Canada would pull its troops out of Afghanistan's Kandahar province
entries.subject: Canadian troops in Kandahar

entries.quote: that Ken Livingstone would be re-elected as mayor of London
entries.subject: London mayoral election 2008

entries.quote: Oh, and we expected that by now Hillary Clinton would be heading for the White House.
entries.subject: US presidential election 2008
entries.note: Restated in the self-review, which adds that the edition also said every election season brings "at least one big surprise".

entries.quote: In politics, as expected, José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero won a second term in Spain.
entries.subject: Spanish general election 2008

entries.quote: And we forecast that China would for the first time overtake the United States in the gold-medal table, with Russia in third place.
entries.subject: Beijing Olympics gold-medal table

notes: Edition number counted from The World in 1987 = 1. Publication month not confirmed; year only. The reprint is The Economist's own web copy of the original article.
